To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the response of thin-window Ge and Si detectors to protons is essentially that of the detector material alone and that the resolution of these detectors is close to the theoretical limit for the material.
the response of thin-window Li-driffed germanium detectors to 29- to 40-MeVa protons has been measured and found to be excellent.
thin-window Li-drifting of Ge and Si is possible and results in detectors with good resolution for long-range particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection and measurement of high-energy protons.
the development of thin-window Li-drifting detectors for the detection of high energy protons.
the development of thin-window Ge detectors for the study of the high-energy end of the proton spectrum in solar flares.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thin-window Li-driffed germanium detector has a resolution for 29-Mev protons which is approximately equal to the theoretical limit for such a device.
thin-window Ge detectors are capable of resolving 29- and/or 40-Mev protons with resolutions of 28 and/or 44 keV, respectively.
the Li-drifted Ge and Si detectors have a resolution for long-range particles which approaches the theoretical limits of these detectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thin-window Ge detectors have been developed to a state where their energy resolutions are comparable to the best available for silicon and Ge detectors.
thin-window Li-drfted Ge and Si detectors have the potential of resolving the 29-Me?v proton line in the? decay of 32 Si.

the thin-window Ge detectors have been shown to be a practical alternative to the conventional Ge(Li) detectors for detecting high-energy protons, while the thin-window Si detectors appear promising for this purpose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thin-window detectors are capable of high-energy proton detection with resolutions comparable to those for electrons.
thin-window germanium detectors can be used to measure the energy of high-energy protons with a resolution of about 1%.
thin-window Li-drifting can produce detectors of very good resolution, which is important when the energy resolution of the detector is comparable to the energy spread in a proton beam.
